study_design: Prospective nested case-control analysis within the ATBC Study, with separate postdiagnosis fatality analyses and ancillary analyses in the entire ATBC cohort
cohort_total_n_excerpt: To investigate possible factors responsible for a spurious association with prostate cancer fatality, we reanalysed baseline serum vitamin D associations with prostate cancer risk and prostate cancer-specific fatality in case-control data nested within the ATBC Study (1000 controls and 1000 incident prostate cancer cases).
reason: The nested case-control component includes 1000 incident prostate cancer cases and analyzes prostate cancer risk both overall and by disease aggressiveness. The prostate cancer-specific fatality analyses are survival outcomes and are not themselves incident aggressive cancer endpoints.

estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied evidence identifies this beta-carotene OR as an incident prostate cancer estimate without an aggressive restriction. It is not classified as survival despite unrelated fatality language appearing in the supplied effect evidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Published analyses of prostate cancer nested case-control and survival data in the Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention (ATBC) Study cohort suggested that men with higher baseline vitamin D [25(OH)D] concentrations have both (i) increased prostate cancer risk and (ii) decreased prostate cancer-specific fatality.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row concerns the overall vitamin D association with prostate cancer risk, distinct from the postdiagnosis fatality analysis and from risk stratified by aggressiveness.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: We replicated these case-control analyses using baseline serum measurements of alpha-tocopherol (vitamin E), beta-carotene and retinol (vitamin A), and used the entire ATBC Study cohort (n = 29 085) to estimate marginal associations between these baseline vitamins and prostate cancer incidence and fatality following blood collection.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row represents the overall vitamin A/retinol incident prostate cancer analysis; it has no stated aggressive endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was positively associated with the highest quintile category of season-specific 25(OH)D in the unstratified analysis (OR = 1.44 for Q5 vs Q1; 95% CI: 1.06, 1.96; P trend = 0.07; Table 2 ).
estimate_classifications.reason: The evidence explicitly calls this an unstratified prostate cancer risk estimate, so it is general rather than aggressive.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Men in the highest quintile category of baseline alpha-tocopherol were less likely to develop prostate cancer during follow-up than men in the lowest quintile category (OR = 0.66 for Q5 vs Q1; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.91; P trend = 0.04; Table 3 ).
estimate_classifications.reason: This alpha-tocopherol estimate concerns development of prostate cancer overall, with no aggressive restriction.
